subject: pe
title: Musculoskeletal System
welcome_lead: Bones, joints and contraction — the architecture of movement.
meta_desc: A-Level PE adventure on muscle structure, contraction and neural control.
final_note: Every movement is sliding filaments multiplied by motor units.

concepts.def: Actin slides over myosin via cross-bridge cycling (Huxley 1954).
One motor neuron and all muscle fibres it innervates.
Two muscles producing opposite movements (e.g., biceps/triceps).
Freely movable joint with capsule and fluid (e.g., hinge, ball-and-socket).
Muscle changes length while producing force (concentric or eccentric).

walkthroughs.body_html: Ca²⁺ exposes actin binding sites; myosin heads bind, swivel, release (powered by ATP).
Henneman size principle: smaller, slower units recruited first; larger, faster units for high force.
Hinge (knee) allows flexion/extension; ball-and-socket (hip) allows movement in all axes.
